Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  
  • 4-day history of severe generalized headache, subjective fever (temperature not measured), generalized myalgias.  
  • Diffuse red, pruritic, blanching rash (positive glass test) developed after headache onset.  
  • Recent return (≈1 week ago) from Thailand with multiple mosquito bites; travel companion also unwell.  
  • No photophobia, no neck stiffness, no vomiting, no focal weakness, no cough/coryza, no earache.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: Severe headache, subjective fever, generalized myalgias, blanching pruritic rash, recent travel to Thailand with mosquito exposure. No meningitic signs on history, but serious tropical or CNS infection cannot be excluded without examination and labs.

Aligned differential diagnoses (from DDx):  
• Dengue fever – High likelihood given travel to Thailand, fever, headache, myalgias, blanching rash emerging days 3-5.  
• Chikungunya virus infection – Moderate likelihood; similar presentation but prominent arthralgias absent.  
• Malaria (P. falciparum) – Moderate likelihood; fever/headache after travel; rash less typical but must be ruled out.  
Additional clinical concern: need to exclude meningitis despite low clinical suspicion (no photophobia/neck stiffness).

Working diagnosis: Probable mosquito-borne viral illness; dengue most likely. Serious infection cannot be excluded without in-person assessment.

Management Plan

- Urgent same-day face-to-face assessment at GP hub; if unavailable, attend emergency department.  
- Physical examination including vitals, focused neuro exam, and rash inspection.  
- Blood tests anticipated: FBC/platelets, LFTs, U&Es, malaria film/RDT, dengue NS1/serology, chikungunya serology, blood cultures if febrile, CRP, other tests per local guidelines.  
- Consider lumbar puncture only if meningitis suspected on examination.  
- Continue symptomatic treatment with paracetamol/ibuprofen as needed (avoid NSAIDs if dengue with thrombocytopenia confirmed).  
- Safety-net advice: seek immediate care for worsening headache, vomiting, bleeding, altered consciousness, non-blanching rash, or inability to access care.  
- Follow-up to review results and clinical status within 24-48 h.

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support): Not recorded.  
- CTG registration: Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Dengue fever – High: Classic presentation and travel history.  
2. Chikungunya virus infection – Moderate: Similar mosquito exposure; less joint pain reported.  
3. Malaria – Moderate: Endemic area exposure; early symptoms nonspecific, needs exclusion.
